text:
maya: noticing a big gap in traces for model-router after last night's exporter rollout — parent spans show up but most child spans (kv-cache, tokenizer) are missing :thinking_face:
jon: ugh, saw alerts from the dashboard at 10:07 UTC — span_drop_rate for model-router jumped to ~35%
maya: yup, console shows exporter v2.0.0 rolling to all runtime nodes around 09:58 UTC
sahil: quick question — are these spans completely absent, or just not linked (parent_id mismatch)?
maya: absent. example trace id 0x8f3a... parent present, no children in the trace view. logs also show OTLP flushes succeeding
elaine: Dumped a few OTLP payloads from one node. looks like the batcher is truncating proto payloads when a graceful shutdown hits a deadline. i saw an error: "failed to encode span: message truncated"
jon: that sounds like https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/… we hit a change in exporter batch handling in v2.0.0 where flush on SIGTERM doesn't wait if queue drained flag set
maya: can you paste the minimal log?
elaine: sure — from model-router-3 log: ```2026-03-17T09:59:12Z WARN exporter/batcher.go:142 drain timeout reached, truncating batch: 12 spans -> 3 spans
2026-03-17T09:59:12Z ERROR exporter/encode.go:87 failed to encode span: proto: unexpected EOF
2026-03-17T09:59:12Z INFO otlp/client.go:204 send ok, items_sent=3```
sahil: that would cause children to get dropped if they were in the truncated part of the batch. if parent was flushed earlier in another batch you get orphaned parents
jon: are we sure this is the rollout? maybe sampling policy changed per-tenant?
maya: checked sampling configs — no changes. rollout window correlates exactly with nodes that got v2.0.0. older nodes still show normal traces
observability-bot: [alert] span_drop_rate > 20% for service=model-router (10:06 — 10:12)
jon: OK rollback plan? we can revert exporter on-canary to v1.2.3 and roll back globally if metrics improve
sahil: before full rollback, can we patch v2.0.0 with a faster drain path? looks like a 100ms deadline in the new batcher default. changing OTEL_EXPORTER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT helps but needs a restart
maya: we pushed a hotfix flag to two nodes: OTEL_EXPORTER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT=5s and restarted. watching dashboard
elaine: after restart those two nodes show span_drop_rate ~2% and traces look complete. the nodes still on default v2 show the 30-40% drop
jon: good repro. action: revert rollout, open a patch PR to increase default drain timeout and add unit test for partial-batch flush on SIGTERM. also add a regression alert for orphaned-parent ratio
maya: created ticket INF-924 and draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/inference-exporter/pull/412 — includes test and config knob OTEL_EXPORTER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT default 5s
sahil: add perf note — longer drain can increase shutdown time; we should also add instrumentation metric exporter.pending_spans_count so alerting can be smarter
elaine: added a quick grafana panel to show pending_spans_count for runtime pods and linked to the incident page
jon: def add an automated canary check that compares trace completeness before promoting an exporter version cluster-wide
maya: noted. will follow up with rollout checklist update (must pass trace-completeness canary for 15m)
observability-bot: [note] incident INF-924 created by maya at 2026-03-17T10:25:00Z
deploy-bot: reverted rollout: inference-exporter v2.0.0 -> v1.2.3 across runtime cluster at 10:31 UTC — monitoring
jon: metrics look back to baseline, span_drop_rate under 1.5% now. closing loop after one hour stable
maya: postmortem items: 1) revert + patch PR 2) add unit/integration test for graceful flush 3) add pending_spans_count metric and alert 4) update rollout checklist for trace completeness canary
sahil: extra: test end-to-end with proto vs json encoders — the truncation surface differed between them so catch both in CI
elaine: leaving a short runbook note in ops-runbooks/trace-exporter.md about the OTEL_EXPORTER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT override and how to debug proto truncation
jon: thanks everyone — nice quick triage. :thumbsup:
maya: recorded a short Loom for customer-facing SREs explaining the rollback and mitigation steps — linking in INF-924
elaine: will follow up with a cleanup PR for the grafana panel and a prometheus metric name proposal
maya: last: add a post-deploy smoke that verifies trace nesting for a synthetic request, otherwise we risk the same silent regression
jon: agreed. closing thread in 1h if stable.
